categories.title: Dental implants
categories.short: A titanium root placed in the jaw, topped with a crown, bridge or denture once the bone has healed around it.
intro: An implant stands in for the lost root of a tooth. Once it has bonded with the jawbone, it can carry a single crown, a bridge across several gaps, or hold a denture firmly in place.

Both of our dentists are prosthodontists and implantologists, so the same team that plans the implant also designs the tooth that sits on it. Not everyone is suited to implants straight away: gum health, bone volume, diabetes and smoking all play a part, and the doctor will talk these through with you.

steps.title: Consultation and scan
steps.text: The doctor examines your mouth, reviews your health and arranges an X-ray or scan to measure the bone.

steps.title: A written plan
steps.text: Options, visit count and costs are written down for you to take home and think over.

steps.title: Placing the implant
steps.text: Done under local anaesthetic. Most people go home the same day with simple aftercare instructions.

steps.title: Healing time
steps.text: The bone usually needs a few months to grow around the implant. A temporary tooth can often be fitted meanwhile.

steps.title: Fitting the final tooth
steps.text: The crown, bridge or denture is made to match and fixed onto the implant, followed by regular reviews.

subTreatments.title: Single-tooth implant
subTreatments.summary: One implant and one crown to fill one gap, without filing down the teeth on either side.
subTreatments.visits: Several visits over a few months

subTreatments.title: Implant-supported bridge
subTreatments.summary: Two or more implants carrying a bridge when several teeth in a row are missing.
subTreatments.visits: Several visits over a few months

subTreatments.title: Implant-retained denture
subTreatments.summary: A small number of implants that clip a denture in place so it no longer slips while eating or talking.
subTreatments.visits: Several visits; depends on the plan

subTreatments.title: Implant consultation
subTreatments.summary: An unhurried first visit to find out whether implants suit you and what the alternatives are.

faqs.q: Am I too old for an implant?
faqs.a: Age alone is rarely the deciding factor. General health, bone and gums matter more, and the doctor will check these with you at the consultation.
A local anaesthetic numbs the site beforehand; patients usually describe pushing or vibration, not pain. The gum may stay tender for a few days; the doctor will suggest which painkiller to take.

categories.title: Crowns, bridges and dentures
categories.short: Rebuilding broken teeth and replacing missing ones with caps, fixed bridges or removable dentures.
intro: This is the core of prosthodontics. A crown is a made-to-measure cap that shields a tooth weakened by a crack, a large filling or root canal work. A bridge fills a gap by anchoring a false tooth to its neighbours. Dentures replace several or all teeth in an arch and can be taken out for cleaning.
The right choice turns on how many gaps you have, how sound your remaining teeth are, and whether you care most about comfort, looks, budget or time in the chair.

steps.title: Examination
steps.text: The doctor checks the teeth and gums and explains which options are realistic for you.

steps.title: Preparation and impressions
steps.text: Teeth are shaped if needed and measured so the new work fits your bite.

steps.title: Trial and fitting
steps.text: Dentures are usually tried in before they are finished; crowns and bridges are checked and cemented.

steps.title: Adjustments
steps.text: A follow-up visit eases any sore spots and fine-tunes the bite.

subTreatments.title: Crowns (caps)
subTreatments.summary: A custom cover that strengthens a weak or broken tooth.

subTreatments.title: Fixed bridges
subTreatments.summary: A false tooth held between crowns on the neighbouring teeth.

subTreatments.title: Complete dentures
subTreatments.summary: A full set of removable teeth when an arch has no natural teeth left.

subTreatments.title: Partial dentures
subTreatments.summary: A removable plate that fills gaps between your remaining teeth.

subTreatments.title: Denture repair and relining
subTreatments.summary: Fixing cracks and refitting loose dentures as the gums change over time.

faqs.q: How long does a new denture take to feel normal?
faqs.a: Many people need a few weeks to get used to speaking and chewing with new dentures. Rubbing spots in the early days are expected, and a quick adjustment visit sorts most of them out.

faqs.q: Crown or implant: which do I need?
faqs.a: A crown saves a tooth you still have; an implant replaces one that is gone. The doctor will tell you whether your tooth can be kept.

categories.title: Check-ups, cleaning and fillings
categories.short: Routine dental checks, scaling with polishing, and white fillings for decay.
intro: Most dental problems are easier and cheaper to sort out when they are small. A routine visit lets the dentist spot early decay, gum inflammation and worn fillings before they start to hurt.
Scaling removes the hardened deposits (tartar) that brushing cannot shift. Small cavities can usually be repaired with a tooth-coloured filling in a single sitting.

steps.title: Talk first
steps.text: Tell the dentist about any pain, sensitivity or bleeding you have noticed.

steps.title: Examination
steps.text: Teeth, gums, old fillings and the bite are checked; an X-ray is taken only if it is needed.

steps.title: Cleaning or filling
steps.text: Done the same day where possible, or booked for a second visit.

steps.title: Home-care advice
steps.text: Simple tips on brushing, flossing and when to come back.

subTreatments.title: Dental check-up
subTreatments.summary: A full look at teeth and gums, with advice on anything that needs attention.

subTreatments.title: Scaling and polishing
subTreatments.summary: Professional cleaning above the gum line to remove tartar and stains.

subTreatments.title: Tooth-coloured fillings
subTreatments.summary: Repairing cavities and chipped edges with a material matched to your tooth shade.

subTreatments.title: Sensitive teeth
subTreatments.summary: Finding the cause of sharp twinges with cold or sweet food and suggesting what may help.

faqs.q: How regularly do I need a dental check?
faqs.a: Twice a year suits many adults. Your dentist may space visits closer or further apart after seeing your teeth and gums.
No. Scaling removes deposits; teeth can feel different afterwards because the tartar that filled the gaps is gone. Any looseness is checked and explained by the dentist.

categories.title: Root canal treatment and extractions
categories.short: Saving an infected tooth by cleaning its canals, or removing a tooth that cannot be kept.
intro: When decay reaches the nerve inside a tooth, it can cause throbbing pain, swelling or a gum boil. Root canal treatment cleans and seals the inside of the tooth so it can usually be kept, often followed by a crown to protect it.
If a tooth is too broken or loose to save, the dentist may advise taking it out, and will talk through how the gap can be filled later with a bridge, denture or implant.

steps.title: Diagnosis
steps.text: An examination and X-ray show whether the tooth can be saved.

steps.title: Numbing
steps.text: Local anaesthetic is given so the procedure is comfortable.

steps.title: Treatment
steps.text: The canals are cleaned and sealed, or the tooth is gently removed.

steps.title: Aftercare
steps.text: You get written instructions and a review visit where needed.

subTreatments.title: Root canal treatment
subTreatments.summary: Cleaning, shaping and sealing the canals of an infected tooth.

subTreatments.title: Tooth removal
subTreatments.summary: Taking out a tooth that cannot be repaired, under local anaesthetic.

subTreatments.title: Planning after an extraction
subTreatments.summary: Discussing options to replace the tooth once the area has healed.

faqs.q: Is a root canal better than taking the tooth out?
faqs.a: Keeping your own tooth is often preferred when it can be saved, but not every tooth can. The dentist will explain the choice for your tooth.

seo.title: Root Canal Treatment & Tooth Removal, Guntur
seo.description: Root canal treatment for infected teeth, gentle extractions and planning to replace a lost tooth at Dent Plus Dental & Family Clinic, Guntur.

categories.title: Children's dental care
categories.short: Friendly first visits, checks on milk teeth and early help with decay and habits.
intro: Baby teeth keep room for the permanent ones underneath and are needed for eating and clear speech, so cavities in them are worth treating. A relaxed first visit, before anything hurts, helps a child see the dental chair as a normal place.
The dentist checks how teeth are coming through, looks for early cavities and gives parents practical advice on brushing, sweets and bottle or thumb habits.

steps.title: Getting comfortable
steps.text: Children can sit on a parent's lap and look at the instruments first.

steps.title: Gentle check

steps.title: Treatment if needed
steps.text: Small fillings or preventive care are explained to both child and parent.

subTreatments.title: Fillings for milk teeth
subTreatments.summary: Repairing small cavities before they cause pain.

subTreatments.title: Advice on habits
subTreatments.summary: Guidance for parents on thumb sucking, night bottles and sugary snacks.

faqs.q: At what age should a child have a first dental visit?
faqs.a: Many dentists suggest a first visit around the time the first teeth appear or by the first birthday. Ask the dentist what suits your child.

categories.title: Smile care
categories.short: Improving the look of chipped, stained, worn or uneven front teeth.
intro: Small changes can make front teeth look neater: rebuilding a chipped edge, replacing old discoloured fillings, or reshaping worn teeth with crowns.
The dentist will tell you honestly what is achievable for your teeth. Results vary from person to person, and healthy gums and teeth always come first.

steps.title: Options

faqs.q: Can you make my teeth whiter?
faqs.a: Surface stains can often be polished away. Whether any further whitening option suits you is something the dentist will advise after checking your teeth.

categories.title: Family medicine
categories.short: A family doctor for everyday illness, check-ups and regular follow-up of long-term conditions.
intro: A family physician is often the first person to see when you feel unwell and are not sure where to go. Our two family physicians see adults and older relatives for fevers, coughs, stomach upsets, aches and general health questions.

For long-term conditions such as high blood pressure or diabetes, regular reviews help you and your doctor notice changes early. When a problem needs tests, a specialist or a hospital, the doctor will explain why and where.

categories.short: Visits for unwell children, growth and feeding questions, and routine checks.
intro: Children fall ill differently from adults, and parents often want to know when to wait and when to worry. A doctor with paediatric training can examine your child, explain what is likely going on and tell you which signs mean you should come back or go to hospital.
Routine visits are also a chance to talk about growth, eating, sleep and vaccinations. This page is general information only; the doctor will advise for your own child.

faqs.a: See our article on children's fevers for general guidance. Babies under three months with a fever, or any child who is very drowsy, struggling to breathe or not drinking, need urgent medical attention.

categories.title: Eye care
categories.short: Eye and vision checks, help with common eye complaints and referral for surgery when needed.
intro: Blurred vision, headaches while reading, red or itchy eyes and difficulty seeing at night are all reasons to have your eyes checked. Our ophthalmology-trained doctor examines the eyes, checks vision and explains what she finds.
Some conditions, such as cataract, may need an operation. In that case the doctor will explain why and refer you to a surgical eye centre. This page is general information only.

faqs.q: Do I need an eye check if I have diabetes?
faqs.a: People with diabetes are often advised to have regular eye checks, because changes can start without symptoms. Ask the doctor how often is right for you.
